chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Salih ibn Sa'id from Yunus from some of his men from some of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about what came in the hadith: 'Pray the Asr prayer when the sun is at the height of one cubit, two cubits, and one foot, and two feet, from this side and from that side.' He asked: 'When is this and how is this, while the shadow may be half a foot at some times?' He said: 'He said 'the shadow of the cubit' and did not say 'the cubit of the shadow', and that is because the shadow of the cubit varies sometimes increasing and sometimes decreasing, while the cubit itself is always a cubit and does not vary.' Then he said: 'One cubit and two cubits and one foot and two feet, so one cubit and two cubits became the explanation of the cubit and two cubits in the time when the shadow of the cubit is one cubit and the shadow of the two cubits is two cubits, so the shadow of the cubit and the two cubits and the cubit and the two cubits are agreed upon in every known time, one explaining the other, confirming it. So when the time is such that the shadow of the cubit is one cubit, the time is one cubit from the shadow of the cubit, and the cubit is one cubit from the shadow. And when the shadow of the cubit is less or more, the time is confined to the cubit and the two cubits. This is the explanation of the cubit and the two cubits and the cubit and the two cubits.' And as for the last part of what we mentioned, which is the time of the necessitated (prayer), it indicates that.

key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: The necessitated (one who missed prayers and must make them up)

ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact time for Asr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction in hadiths regarding Asr prayer times by distinguishing between the variable length of the shadow and the constant standard of measurement, thereby linking the 'cubit' and 'foot' references to specific shadow lengths. This explanation establishes a flexible yet precise jurisprudential method for determining the onset of Asr, accommodating geographical and seasonal variations in shadow length while maintaining ritual consistency. The clarification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on reconciling textual ambiguities through logical deduction and practical application in daily worship.
